history.period: Present structure ~early 20th century (about 100 years old); worship tradition revived ~500 years ago; legend traced to Treta Yuga
history.summary: The town Janki Temple at Sitamarhi is a modern (~100-year-old) shrine marking the spot where, per Ramayana tradition, King Janaka found the infant Sita while ploughing and later installed stone figures of Rama, Sita and Lakshmana; the figures were reportedly lost to jungle and re-discovered by the ascetic Birbal Das of Ayodhya about 500 years ago, who cleared the site and resumed worship. The adjacent Janaki Kund tank (south of the temple) is traditionally where Janaka bathed the infant Sita. CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column holds the town name 'Sitamarhi'; the real state is Bihar. NOTE: several sources conflate this town temple with Punaura Dham (5 km west), which has its own separate record here; a distinct Janaki Sthan mandir ~2 km away also claims the birthplace, so identity details are kept to what is reliably reported for the town shrine.

name: Janki Temple
town_description: Sitamarhi is a town in northern Bihar near the Nepal border, at the heart of the Mithila region. It is famous as the traditional birthplace of Sita, wife of Rama, and is a major Hindu pilgrimage centre, with several shrines around the town claiming association with Sita's birth. It is about 130 km from Patna and 60 km from Janakpur, Nepal.
